text:
Maria.Ng: Heads up — commitment renewals are coming up next month. We need a refreshed GPU reserved-capacity forecast for hosted API vs committed supply. Early signals: hosted text gen QPS +18% MoM, embeddings +45% on the same fleet.

Josh: Do we have a baseline window? last 30d P95 usage and current committed vGPU count?

Maria.Ng: Baseline = rolling 30d average GPU-hours from hosted pool. Current committed supply = 2,400 vGPU-hours/day (US-W / EU-C combined). Need full split by region.

Deepak: Also important: effective throughput per vGPU improved after the 2.1 runtime patches (better batching + kernel selection). That reduces raw vGPU needs by ~8% for text-gen tails. But embedding throughput still dominates because of CPU pre/post.

Emily-Fin: flagging a billing oddity — last invoice didn't apply the committed discount for the US-W reserved pool (invoice INV-2026-031). Can someone check mapping of commitment IDs to billing accounts? @finance-bot included.

finance-bot: Automated check: commitment ID RWI-comm-324 shows active in our commitment ledger. Billing reconciliation pending manual review (expected ETA 24h).

ops-bot: New capacity summary uploaded: https://internal.redwood/capacity/reports/1768001234 (contains per-region histograms + reserved vs hosted split).

Maria.Ng: Quick sketch of the gap (very rough) — sharing as code block:

```
period, hosted_forecast_gpu_hours, committed_gpu_hours, delta
2026-04, 3100, 2400, +700
2026-05, 3350, 2400, +950
2026-06, 3600, 2400, +1200
```

Josh: OK. Propose scenario runs:
- Scenario A (conservative): renew current commitment, add 300 vGPU-hours/day burst buffer (on-demand).
- Scenario B (aggressive): increase committed pool by 20% (approx +480 vGPU-hrs/day), negotiate price tier.
- Scenario C (optimize): keep current commit, commit to cross-region flexibility (shift 30% EU<->US), buy short-term reservations for predicted peaks.

Deepak: For Scenario B, we need to model utilization curves. If utilization < 75% for more than 3 consecutive months, we bleed savings. I'll run sims with per-model token-level cost and runtime improvements.

Emily-Fin: For finance approval we need: expected committed spend by month, burn-rate impact, and fallback plan (on-demand+spot) to limit downside. Also note contract windows: 12/24/36 month options and early termination penalties if any.

Maria.Ng: Action items:
- @Deepak: run utilization sims and produce per-scenario vGPU need + cost delta (deadline: 48h).
- @Josh: draft negotiation asks for +20% increase (target price tiers, SLA asks) and gather committed-negotiate leads (deadline: 72h).
- @Emily-Fin: start pre-check on invoice mapping and potential credit if billing missed discounts (ETA: 24h).

Deepak: ACK. I'll attach the sim notebook and include sensitivity tests for embedding-heavy customers and a worst-case +30% demand spike. Will also include regional breakdown.

Josh: Also one more ask — can we test prioritized routing to dedicated fleet for high-value customers to reduce hosted tail pressure? If we can shift 5–10% of high QPS traffic to dedicated, that helps the host pool gap.

Maria.Ng: Good point. Add routing experiment to the sims. If routing reduces peak-hosted demand by 8% we might avoid a full commitment bump.

finance-bot: Invoice check: billing team acknowledged INV-2026-031 discrepancy; tentative credit hold flagged. ETA for reversal/credit: 3–5 business days.

Emily-Fin: Thanks. Also please include the "effective $/token" metric per scenario so we can compare to existing reserved pricing lanes.

Maria.Ng: OK team — let's reconvene in the channel with the sim outputs. Target decision meeting with Eng+Finance in one week. Please ping @Josh and @Emily-Fin once your docs are up. :thumbsup:

Deepak: Will post sim outputs to the report link and drop a short summary here when done.

Josh: Will coordinate with sales for customer routing opt-in tests.

Maria.Ng: Closing — thanks everyone.
